annotations.description: Keeping a 7-card hand with zero colored mana sources. The hand has Urza's Factory, Urza's Mine, and Urza's Tower (without Power-Plant so no Tron bonus), producing only colorless mana. The deck needs white and blue mana for its spells (Inspiring Overseer, Drownyard Explorers, Blessed Sanctuary, Flicker of Fate, etc.). Planar Atlas can dig for a colored land, but that's only looking at 4 cards with no guarantee.
annotations.actionTaken: Kept a 7-card hand with 3 colorless-only lands and 4 artifacts, no colored mana sources.
annotations.betterLine: Mulligan to 6 looking for a hand with at least one colored mana source. While going to 6 is a cost, having zero colored mana makes most of the deck's spells uncastable. The Planar Atlas dig is a partial out but unreliable.

annotations.description: GPT54 Sport passed with 2 untapped Plains and no other way to spend mana this turn (all cards in hand cost 3+, no lands in hand). Valorous Stance could destroy the 2/4 Drownyard Explorers for free since the mana would otherwise go completely unused. While saving removal for a bigger threat has merit, the opponent's 2/4 is a reasonable body that can block, and wasting 2 mana entirely is a real cost.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting the investigate trigger resolve and keeping Valorous Stance in hand with 2 mana unused this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Valorous Stance targeting Drownyard Explorers to remove the 2/4 body. The investigate trigger would still resolve, but removing the creature for otherwise-wasted mana could be worthwhile. Alternatively, holding for a bigger threat or indestructible mode on a future Emiel/Overseer is defensible.

annotations.description: GPT54 Sport passed with 2 open mana and Valorous Stance in hand, which could destroy the opponent's Drownyard Explorers (toughness 4). With no board presence and no other productive use for the mana this turn, removing the opponent's only creature would have been a clean tempo play. The opponent's Explorers already got its investigate ETB, so it's just a 2/4 body that will attack/block in future turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority with 2 untapped Plains, wasting the mana for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Valorous Stance targeting Drownyard Explorers (toughness 4) to destroy it, removing the opponent's only creature while having no competing use for the mana this turn.

annotations.description: Discarded Blessed Sanctuary, which forms a powerful combo with Emiel the Blessed already in hand. With Emiel + Blessed Sanctuary, every creature flicker generates a 2/2 Unicorn token (which Emiel puts two +1/+1 counters on for just {G/W}). This is a game-winning engine with all the ETB creatures in the hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Blessed Sanctuary
annotations.betterLine: Discard Valorous Steed - it's the least impactful card at 5 mana (just a 3/3 vigilance + 2/2 token), while Blessed Sanctuary creates a dominant synergy engine with Emiel the Blessed and all the ETB creatures in hand.

annotations.description: Cast Walking Ballista for X=2 (a 2/2) when Magnifying Glass would have been better. With Urza's Power Plant in hand and Tron about to come online next turn, Magnifying Glass provides mana ramp that would allow a much larger Ballista (X=5 as a 5/5) next turn. The opponent has no creatures and only 2 Plains, so there's no urgency for a 2/2 body. Magnifying Glass also offers long-term card draw utility.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Walking Ballista for X=2 as a 2/2
annotations.betterLine: Cast Magnifying Glass for 3 mana (leaving 1 unused), then next turn with Tron complete + Magnifying Glass, cast a much larger Walking Ballista (X=4 or 5) with the 9-10 available mana.

annotations.description: Walking Ballista is on the stack and will enter as a 4/4 (toughness 4+). The player chose to cast Valorous Stance now, but the only legal target with toughness 4+ on the battlefield is Drownyard Explorers (2/4). Killing the Explorers is far less impactful than saving Valorous Stance to destroy the Walking Ballista after it resolves, since Ballista can repeatedly ping creatures and the player for damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Valorous Stance while Walking Ballista was on the stack, likely targeting Drownyard Explorers instead of the much more dangerous incoming Ballista.
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority, let Walking Ballista resolve and enter the battlefield as a 4/4, then cast Valorous Stance to destroy it before the opponent can remove counters to deal damage.

annotations.description: Activated Walking Ballista to remove a +1/+1 counter to deal 1 damage to an opponent at 20 life with no creatures to target. The Ballista is sick this turn so can't attack, but shrinking it from 4/4 to 3/3 for just 1 point of damage is a poor trade when the opponent has 20 life and no board threats to pick off.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Walking Ballista to remove a counter and ping for 1 damage
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority and keep the Ballista at 4/4 for future combat. The 1 damage is negligible against 20 life and the counter is more valuable on the creature.

annotations.description: Walking Ballista is about to be destroyed by Valorous Stance. One 'ping' activation is already on the stack, but the Ballista still has 3 more +1/+1 counters that could be converted to 3 damage before it dies. By passing, all 3 remaining counters (3 damage) are wasted when Valorous Stance resolves and destroys the Ballista.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Walking Ballista again, letting it die with 3 unused +1/+1 counters.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Walking Ballista's 'remove a +1/+1 counter: deal 1 damage' ability three more times in response, targeting the opponent (or relevant permanents), to extract all 4 total damage before Valorous Stance resolves and destroys it.

annotations.description: Walking Ballista is about to be destroyed by Valorous Stance. GPT52 Nature had 2 remaining +1/+1 counters on Walking Ballista (after the one already on the stack) that could each be removed to deal 1 damage before it dies. By passing, those counters are wasted when the Ballista is destroyed.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority with Walking Ballista's activated ability available, letting Valorous Stance resolve and destroy the Ballista with 2 unused counters.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Walking Ballista's 'remove a +1/+1 counter: deal 1 damage' ability two more times (targeting the opponent or a relevant permanent) to extract all remaining value before the Ballista is destroyed.

annotations.description: Walking Ballista already had one ping on the stack targeting Inspiring Overseer (a 2/1). One damage is lethal to a 1-toughness creature. By activating the second counter removal, the player dealt redundant overkill damage and reduced Walking Ballista to 0/0, killing it via state-based actions. The Ballista would have survived as a 1/1 and could have been grown later with its {4} pump ability, especially valuable with Tron lands online.
annotations.actionTaken: Removed the second +1/+1 counter from Walking Ballista to deal a redundant 1 damage to Inspiring Overseer, killing the Ballista.
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority and let the first ping resolve, killing Inspiring Overseer with 1 damage. Walking Ballista survives as a 1/1 with future growth potential.

annotations.description: Player passed priority in precombat main phase with Magnifying Glass castable. With Mechanized Production in hand (which needs to enchant an artifact and wants 8+ artifacts with the same name), deploying Magnifying Glass builds toward the win condition. Magnifying Glass also provides ramp and card draw via investigate, which is valuable with Tron assembled.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything, effectively ending the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Magnifying Glass to add another artifact to the board, setting up Mechanized Production next turn. Magnifying Glass is an excellent enchant target for Mechanized Production since copied Magnifying Glasses provide mana and investigation while counting toward the 8-artifact win condition.

annotations.description: Faith's Fetters was used on a Walking Ballista with only 1 +1/+1 counter (a 1/1 that can deal at most 1 damage), while the opponent has Urza's Factory plus all three Tron lands (Mine, Power Plant, Tower). Once Tron is fully online, Factory generates 2/2 tokens repeatedly for just {7} (which Tron provides from 3 lands alone). Faith's Fetters on Factory would shut down both its mana production and token generation permanently.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Walking Ballista (1/1) with Faith's Fetters
annotations.betterLine: Target Urza's Factory with Faith's Fetters to neutralize the opponent's primary long-term win condition and token generation engine, especially with Tron pieces all in play

annotations.description: Opponent's creatures are both summoning sick and cannot block. Attacking with only Drownyard Explorers (2 damage) instead of also Runed Servitor (additional 2 damage) wastes 2 free damage when opponent is at 10 life. There's no downside to attacking with Runed Servitor since nothing can block it.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Drownyard Explorers for 2 damage
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Drownyard Explorers and Runed Servitor for 4 total damage, bringing opponent to 6 life instead of 8. All opponent creatures are summoning sick so there's zero risk.

annotations.description: Blocked Drownyard Explorers (2/4) with Gallant Cavalry (2/2), which results in losing Gallant Cavalry without killing the attacker. At 10 life, taking 2 to go to 8 is manageable, and Gallant Cavalry has enormous value as an Emiel the Blessed blink target (each blink creates a 2/2 Knight token). Alternatively, double-blocking with both Gallant Cavalry and Knight Token would actually kill the Explorers.
annotations.actionTaken: Single-blocked Drownyard Explorers with Gallant Cavalry, losing it without trading.
annotations.betterLine: Either don't block (take 2 damage, preserve Gallant Cavalry for Emiel blink value), or double-block with both Gallant Cavalry and Knight Token to actually kill the Explorers. Not blocking is likely best since Gallant Cavalry as an Emiel target generates repeated 2/2 tokens.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main with Press for Answers in hand and Emiel the Blessed (a 4/4 with powerful blink ability) as a prime target. Also had mana to activate Floodhound for additional artifact generation (relevant for Mechanized Production in hand). Emiel untapped threatens to generate massive ETB value next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 5 untapped lands and multiple useful actions available.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Press for Answers targeting Emiel the Blessed to tap it down for a turn cycle and create a Clue token, then activate Floodhound to investigate with remaining mana, building toward Mechanized Production's artifact count.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 10 life with only a single untapped blocker (Knight Token 2/2) and all lands tapped (no combat tricks possible). Emiel the Blessed is summoning sick and can't block. Attacking with multiple creatures would guarantee at least 2-5 damage getting through, applying critical pressure against a 10-life opponent.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack, passing combat with no attackers declared.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with at least Drownyard Explorers and Runed Servitor (and likely Floodhound too). With only one blocker available and no mana for tricks, 2-5 damage would get through for free, putting the opponent to 5-8 life and setting up a potential lethal next turn.

annotations.description: Targeted opponent's Emiel the Blessed (4/4) with Daybreak Charger's +2/+0 ETB trigger, making it a 6/4, instead of targeting one of their own creatures to improve their combat position.
annotations.actionTaken: Gave +2/+0 to opponent's Emiel the Blessed, buffing it to 6/4
annotations.betterLine: Target own Drownyard Explorers (becoming 4/4) or Runed Servitor (becoming 4/2) to improve attack potential against opponent at 10 life

annotations.description: Flicker of Fate was cast in response to the opponent's Alchemist's Vial ability targeting Emiel the Blessed. Flickering Emiel would have made it a new object, causing the Vial ability to fizzle and keeping Emiel free to attack/block. Instead, they targeted Assembly-Worker Token, which is a token — when exiled by Flicker of Fate, it ceases to exist and never returns. This wastes the Flicker of Fate, permanently destroys their own token, and leaves Emiel locked down.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Assembly-Worker Token with Flicker of Fate, destroying their own token for no benefit.
annotations.betterLine: Target Emiel the Blessed with Flicker of Fate to counter the Alchemist's Vial ability, keeping Emiel free to attack and triggering its ETB ability.

annotations.description: Daybreak Charger's ETB +2/+0 was placed on Knight Token instead of Emiel the Blessed. Both lines produce 8 total attack damage, but if the opponent blocks with Drownyard Explorers (2/4), a pumped Knight Token (4/2) trades with it while a pumped Emiel (6/4) kills it and survives. Pumping Emiel preserves board presence in any blocking scenario.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Knight Token with Daybreak Charger's +2/+0 ETB trigger
annotations.betterLine: Target Emiel the Blessed with +2/+0, making it a 6/4 attacker that survives any block from the opponent's creatures

annotations.description: At 10 life, holding back Emiel the Blessed 4/4 is overly conservative. The opponent's potential crack-back (Drownyard Explorers 2/4 + Floodhound 1/2 + Runed Servitor 2/2 = 5 power) isn't lethal even without Emiel blocking, and Daybreak Charger can block. Meanwhile, the opponent is building an artifact/card advantage engine with Magnifying Glass, Urza's Factory, and Floodhound that will take over if the game goes long.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Knight Token (4/2 vigilance), holding back Emiel the Blessed
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Emiel the Blessed and Knight Token for 8 potential damage. Even if opponent blocks Emiel with Drownyard Explorers, you trade favorably and still get 4 through with the Knight. Pressuring the opponent's life total is critical before their engine takes over.

annotations.description: Blocked with Drownyard Explorers (2/4) instead of Runed Servitor (2/2) against the 4/2 Knight Token. Both creatures trade with the Knight either way, but Drownyard Explorers is the more valuable body to keep — it's a better blocker against the opponent's Emiel the Blessed (4/4) and other threats. Runed Servitor's death trigger (each player draws a card) is roughly neutral.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked the 4/2 Knight Token with Drownyard Explorers (2/4), trading away the better body.
annotations.betterLine: Block with Runed Servitor (2/2) instead. Both still trade with the 4/2 Knight Token, but you preserve the 2/4 Explorers as a more impactful blocker for future turns. The mutual card draw from Runed Servitor's death is acceptable.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Floodhound's investigate ability before combat. With Mechanized Production in hand (which enchants an artifact and wins with 8+ same-named artifacts), creating Clue tokens is directly advancing the win condition. Floodhound is only a 1/2 and has minimal combat relevance against the opponent's board.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities, moving to combat.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Floodhound ({3}, {T}: Investigate) using Urza's Power Plant + Magnifying Glass + Urza's Factory to create a Clue token, building toward the Mechanized Production artifact-copying win condition.

annotations.description: Passed priority in precombat main with Tron assembled and Urza's Factory available to activate. With opponent at 9 life and all their creatures/lands tapped, creating a 2/2 Assembly-Worker token would add to the board at no real cost. Could also have used Floodhound or Magnifying Glass to investigate. Instead, all that mana went to waste.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without taking any action, wasting a full turn's worth of Tron mana.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Urza's Factory ({7}, {T}) to create a 2/2 Assembly-Worker token, and potentially also activate Floodhound to investigate if mana allowed. Building the board while the opponent is tapped out is critical.

annotations.description: Passed priority in precombat main with 6 mana available and multiple useful actions. Could have activated Floodhound to investigate (creating a Clue artifact token for future use with Filigree Attendant/Mechanized Production), and/or activated Locthwain Gargoyle to attack as a 2/3 flyer against an opponent at 9 life with tapped creatures. Could also cast Thaumaturge's Familiar (3 mana artifact flyer with scry). All of these could still be done postcombat, but activating Gargoyle specifically needed to happen precombat to enable an attack.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without taking any action
annotations.betterLine: Activate Locthwain Gargoyle for 4 mana to get a 2/3 flyer, then attack with it into the opponent at 9 life (Emiel is tapped, only untapped blockers are sick). Use remaining 2 mana postcombat or activate Floodhound instead if preferring the Clue.

annotations.description: Opponent at 9 life with all creatures either tapped or summoning sick, meaning no blockers available. Floodhound could have attacked for 1 free, unblocked damage. While only 1 damage, it's completely risk-free and the opponent is at a relatively low life total.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed combat without declaring any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Floodhound for 1 free unblocked damage, bringing opponent from 9 to 8 life.

annotations.description: Settle Beyond Reality says 'Choose one or both' but GPT54 Sport only chose mode 1 (exile opponent's creature), declining the free mode 2 (blink own creature). Blinking Valorous Steed would create a free 2/2 Knight token with vigilance, and Emiel the Blessed could put two +1/+1 counters on the returning Unicorn for {W}. This is pure upside that was left on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected only mode 1 (exile target creature you don't control) for Settle Beyond Reality
annotations.betterLine: Select both modes — exile an opponent's creature AND blink Valorous Steed to generate a 2/2 Knight token (and potentially get +1/+1 counters from Emiel)

annotations.description: With the opponent at 18 life and all their lands tapped (unable to cast combat tricks or activate Locthwain Gargoyle's ability), attacking with only a 2/2 Knight Token applies minimal pressure. The opponent's board has only Floodhound 1/2 and Locthwain Gargoyle 0/3 - very weak offensively - so keeping Emiel back as a blocker is unnecessary. Attacking with both Emiel and the Knight would force the opponent to make difficult blocking decisions and deal significantly more damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Knight Token (2/2)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Emiel the Blessed (4/4) and Knight Token (2/2) to deal up to 6 damage. With all opponent lands tapped, there's no risk of combat tricks, and the opponent's offensive capability is minimal so defensive concerns are low.

annotations.description: Could have attacked with Locthwain Gargoyle after pumping it for 4 mana to get a 2/3 flyer past the opponent's ground creatures, dealing 2 damage to an opponent at 9 life. The opponent has no flyers to block. However, this would leave only 2 mana for the second main phase, potentially preventing casting of Mechanized Production (4 mana) or Thaumaturge's Familiar (3 mana).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed combat without attacking.
annotations.betterLine: Pump Locthwain Gargoyle for 4 mana and attack for 2 flying damage. At 9 life, chip damage is relevant, especially since the opponent's board is growing with Emiel generating value. Could cast post-combat plays on subsequent turns instead.

annotations.description: With Tron online providing ~9 mana from 6 untapped lands, GPT52 could have activated Locthwain Gargoyle for {4} to give it +2/+0 and flying, then attacked for 2 unblockable damage against an opponent at 9 life with no flyers. Missing 2 free damage in a game where the opponent is building a board with Emiel flicker value is meaningful.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without activating Locthwain Gargoyle or using any abilities.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Locthwain Gargoyle for {4} to make it a 2/3 flyer, then attack with it for 2 unblockable flying damage, bringing the opponent to 7 life.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main with full Tron assembled and multiple mana sinks available. Could have activated Urza's Factory (7 mana + tap) to create a 2/2 token for board presence, or at minimum used Floodhound ({3},{T}) or Magnifying Glass ({4},{T}) to investigate for card advantage. Instead, all that mana went to waste.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities, wasting all available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Urza's Factory to create a 2/2 Assembly-Worker token (using Tron lands for 6 + Planar Atlas for 1 = 7 mana, then tap Factory). This builds board presence against the opponent's growing army while still holding up Islands for Jace's Scrutiny if needed.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main phase with 4 untapped lands and a castable Thaumaturge's Familiar (3 mana, 1/3 flyer with scry 1) in hand, plus Floodhound's investigate ability available. Against an opponent with Emiel the Blessed 4/4 and multiple creatures threatening lethal, deploying a flying blocker and getting scry value is significant. The mana was completely wasted.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn without spending any mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Thaumaturge's Familiar for {3} to add a 1/3 flying blocker and scry 1, or at minimum activate Floodhound to investigate and build artifact count for future Mechanized Production / Filigree Attendant value.

annotations.description: Passed the turn with 2 untapped mana and a Clue token available to sacrifice for a card draw. Drawing a card here is pure upside with no reason to hold the mana (turn is ending). Jace's Scrutiny was also castable and would create another artifact (relevant for Mechanized Production in hand).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 2 mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Clue Token to sacrifice it and draw a card for {2}. Alternatively, cast Jace's Scrutiny on an opponent's creature to investigate and build artifact count for Mechanized Production.

annotations.description: Cast Jace's Scrutiny in postcombat main phase where the -4/-0 effect is completely wasted (expires at end of this turn, before opponent's combat). This essentially pays 2 mana for a Clue token. The alternative — cracking the existing Clue token for 2 mana — would draw a card immediately rather than requiring an additional 2 mana investment later.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Jace's Scrutiny in postcombat main, wasting the -4/-0 text and creating a Clue that costs 2 more mana to convert to a card.
annotations.betterLine: Activate the existing Clue Token for {2} to draw a card immediately. This provides an actual card now instead of a Clue token that requires 2 more mana to crack later. The Scrutiny could be saved for the opponent's combat phase where the -4/-0 would actually reduce damage.

annotations.description: Blocked the Valorous Steed 3/3 with Thaumaturge's Familiar 1/3, causing the Familiar to die. By instead blocking both Knight Tokens 2/2, both blockers (0/3 Gargoyle and 1/3 Familiar) would have survived since neither Knight has enough power to kill them. The player took 2 damage instead of 3 but lost a 1/3 flying creature unnecessarily.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked a Knight Token with Gargoyle and Valorous Steed with Thaumaturge's Familiar, losing the Familiar and taking 2 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block both Knight Tokens with Gargoyle and Familiar respectively. Both blockers survive (0/3 and 1/3 vs 2 power each), take 3 from unblocked Valorous Steed, but keep both creatures on board.

annotations.description: Cast Mechanized Production into an opponent who has Emiel the Blessed + Rambunctious Mutt on the battlefield. The opponent can flicker Mutt for just {3} to destroy the enchantment immediately on their turn. This wastes the card for essentially no value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mechanized Production (which will be destroyed next turn by Emiel flickering Rambunctious Mutt)
annotations.betterLine: Play Urza's Power Plant first (land drop), then use mana on Urza's Factory activation (create 2/2 token), Floodhound investigate, crack Clue tokens, or activate Magnifying Glass to generate card advantage and board presence rather than waste Mechanized Production into guaranteed removal.

annotations.description: Opponent has Mechanized Production on the battlefield, which threatens to win the game by accumulating 8 same-named artifacts. GPT54 Sport had exactly 6 mana to cast Wispweaver Angel (4/4 flying), which could blink Rambunctious Mutt to destroy Mechanized Production. Instead, they cast the much lower-impact Distinguished Conjurer (1/2), failing to address the urgent alternate win condition while also deploying a far weaker creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Distinguished Conjurer (1/2 for 2 mana), leaving Mechanized Production unchecked.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wispweaver Angel for 6 mana, targeting Rambunctious Mutt with its ETB trigger to blink it and destroy Mechanized Production, simultaneously deploying a 4/4 flyer.

annotations.description: Opponent has Mechanized Production on the battlefield, which will create artifact copies each upkeep and win the game at 8 same-named artifacts. Opponent already has 2 Clue tokens and 6 total artifacts, so the win condition is approaching fast. GPT54 Sport has Rambunctious Mutt (destroys artifact or enchantment on ETB) and two ways to blink it: Acrobatic Maneuver or Emiel the Blessed's ability, both costing 3 mana with 4 Plains untapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without acting, leaving Mechanized Production in play to generate more tokens toward the alternate win condition.
annotations.betterLine: Use Emiel the Blessed's activated ability (3 mana) to blink Rambunctious Mutt, triggering its ETB to destroy Mechanized Production. This removes the alternate win condition threat. Alternatively, cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Rambunctious Mutt for the same effect plus drawing a card (even better since it's card advantage).

annotations.description: Casting Acrobatic Maneuver while Distinguished Conjurer is still on the stack means the flickered creature re-enters before Distinguished Conjurer is on the battlefield, missing the 'whenever another creature enters, gain 1 life' trigger. At 9 life against a Mechanized Production clock, every point matters.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Acrobatic Maneuver with Distinguished Conjurer still on the stack
annotations.betterLine: Let Distinguished Conjurer resolve first (pass priority), then cast Acrobatic Maneuver targeting Rambunctious Mutt to destroy Mechanized Production while also gaining 1 life from Distinguished Conjurer's trigger

annotations.description: Blocked Emiel the Blessed with Floodhound (1/2), which dies for minimal value (1 damage to Emiel). Floodhound is a useful repeatable investigate engine. Could have instead let Floodhound stay unblocking and used Gargoyle to chump Emiel, taking 2 more damage (going to 9 instead of 11) but preserving the more valuable utility creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Locthwain Gargoyle blocks Knight Token, Floodhound blocks Emiel the Blessed - losing Floodhound to save 2 life
annotations.betterLine: Block Emiel with Locthwain Gargoyle (chump block, Gargoyle dies) and leave Floodhound unblocked. Take 7 damage (go to 9) but preserve the repeatable investigate engine which is more valuable long-term than the 0/3 Gargoyle.

annotations.description: GPT52 Nature has enough mana to both cast Shambling Suit (3 mana) AND activate Urza's Factory (7 mana + tap), but only chose to activate Factory. With Tron assembled plus other mana sources totaling ~13 mana from non-Factory permanents, both plays are easily affordable. Shambling Suit would enter as roughly a 5/3 or 6/3 (counting artifacts), which is a much-needed blocker/attacker given the opponent's board pressure and Nature being at only 11 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Urza's Factory to create a 2/2 token without casting Shambling Suit from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Shambling Suit first (3 mana), then activate Urza's Factory (7 mana + tap) to deploy both a large Shambling Suit and a 2/2 Assembly-Worker token in the same turn.

annotations.description: GPT52 Nature declined to attack with Locthwain Gargoyle when they had enough mana to activate it as a 2/3 flier. The opponent at 10 life has no fliers to block, all lands tapped, and 3 cards in hand but no mana to cast them. With 0 cards in hand, GPT52 has limited uses for the mana otherwise. They could activate Gargoyle for 4 mana and still crack the Clue for 2 mana to draw a card.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack, passing the combat phase entirely.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Locthwain Gargoyle for {4} to make it a 2/3 flier and attack for 2 unblockable damage, bringing the opponent to 8 life. Then crack the Clue token with remaining mana to draw a card.

annotations.description: Casting Faith's Fetters precombat when the likely target (Shambling Suit 5/3) is summoning sick and can't block this turn anyway. Attacking first would be free information and avoids telegraphing the play before combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Faith's Fetters in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Go to combat first, attack with the full board (Shambling Suit can't block since it's sick), then cast Faith's Fetters postcombat on Shambling Suit or another key permanent. This preserves all options and doesn't reveal information before attacks.

annotations.description: With Faith's Fetters on the stack and 3 untapped Plains, GPT54 Sport could have activated Emiel the Blessed ({3}) to flicker Rambunctious Mutt, which would trigger its ETB to destroy an additional artifact/enchantment (like Magnifying Glass, a key mana/card advantage source for the opponent) and gain 1 life from Distinguished Conjurer's trigger. This is free value since the mana would otherwise go unused.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emiel the Blessed, leaving 3 mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emiel the Blessed targeting Rambunctious Mutt for {3}, destroying an opponent's artifact like Magnifying Glass on re-entry while gaining 1 life from Distinguished Conjurer.

annotations.description: Player passed with 4 untapped mana and no cards in hand, missing the opportunity to activate Locthwain Gargoyle ({4}: +2/+0 and flying) for a 2-damage flying attack against an opponent at 10 life. Since Faith's Fetters is about to lock down Shambling Suit and the player has no other plays, using the mana on the Gargoyle activation to chip in 2 flying damage is clearly better than wasting the mana entirely.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority with 4 untapped lands and no other plays available, wasting all mana for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Locthwain Gargoyle for {4} to give it +2/+0 and flying, then attack for 2 damage in the air, putting opponent to 8 life.

annotations.description: With Faith's Fetters on the stack and 3 untapped Plains available, GPT54 Sport could have activated Emiel the Blessed to blink Rambunctious Mutt, destroying one of the opponent's artifacts or enchantments (Magnifying Glass, Planar Atlas, or Clue Token) while also gaining 1 life from Distinguished Conjurer's trigger. In a close game at 10 vs 11 life, destroying a mana-producing artifact from an Urza-lands opponent is highly impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emiel the Blessed, wasting 3 available mana and missing a free ETB trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emiel the Blessed targeting Rambunctious Mutt (3 mana). When Mutt re-enters, destroy an opponent's artifact (likely Magnifying Glass or Planar Atlas to deny mana), gain 1 life from Distinguished Conjurer, then let Faith's Fetters resolve on Shambling Suit.

annotations.description: GPT54 Sport passed with 3 untapped Plains and Emiel the Blessed's ability available, missing the opportunity to blink Rambunctious Mutt to destroy another of the opponent's artifacts (like Magnifying Glass, which provides both mana and card draw). This would also trigger Distinguished Conjurer for 1 life gain.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emiel the Blessed
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emiel the Blessed targeting Rambunctious Mutt (cost {3}) to get another ETB trigger destroying an opponent's artifact like Magnifying Glass, while also gaining 1 life from Distinguished Conjurer's trigger.

annotations.description: GPT54 Sport passed with 3 untapped Plains and Emiel the Blessed available. They could have activated Emiel to blink Rambunctious Mutt, triggering its ETB to destroy an opponent's artifact (like Magnifying Glass, which provides both mana and card advantage via investigate). This also would have triggered Distinguished Conjurer for 1 life gain. This is significant free value that was left on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Emiel the Blessed
annotations.betterLine: Activate Emiel the Blessed targeting Rambunctious Mutt (spending 3 Plains), then on re-entry destroy Magnifying Glass (opponent's mana rock and investigate engine), gaining 1 life from Distinguished Conjurer

annotations.description: Passed on cracking the Clue Token before combat. With 2 untapped mana and no other spells castable this turn (Wispweaver Angel costs 6), cracking the Clue to draw before declaring attacks would provide maximum information for combat decisions.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating the Clue Token
annotations.betterLine: Activate the Clue Token for {2} to draw a card before combat, potentially finding a combat trick or useful information to inform attack decisions.
